candidate.title: 3Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina schematic of 3′-end Sequencing for Expression Quantification (3Seq; 3SEQ in the primary paper), specifically the single partially degraded FFPE-RNA route. It begins with RNA fragments, enriches poly(A)-bearing 3′ fragments, and constructs directional P5/P7-linked double-stranded cDNA through primer annealing, reverse transcription, second-strand synthesis and P5 ligation. The leftmost title pictogram is descriptive; no alternative workflow or branch is drawn. The graph ends at cDNA. Text-reported downstream PCR and P5-initiated sequencing clarify the readout interface without adding unshown operations, conditions or analysis settings.

states.label: Partially degraded RNA from FFPE sample
features: Partially degraded RNA from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue is the process input.
The interrupted purple strand represents degradation; AA(A)n marks a surviving poly(A) end in the illustrated RNA population.
The scoped FFPE route uses already-short RNA without further fragmentation, as resolved by the primary Figure 1 caption.

states.label: P5/P7-linked double-stranded cDNA endpoint
features: Blue duplex carries magenta P5 on one end and orange P7 on the opposite end; the following simplified cDNA icon marks the endpoint.
P7 is adjacent to the copied poly(A) end; P5 lies toward the upstream transcript-derived end.
cDNA is the carrier that will be amplified and sequenced to represent polyadenylated RNA 3′ regions.
The reported downstream interface is PCR through P5/P7 followed by sequencing from P5 toward the poly(A) end, yielding 3′-biased transcript tags for expression quantification.
Mapped tag counts support transcript/gene abundance estimates. The primary paper presents one tag per transcript as the design goal for reducing transcript-length bias.
Internal priming and polymerase slippage limit the intended 3′ targeting; selection and oligo(dT) priming do not establish perfect end specificity.

operations.label: Poly(A) selection (poly A selected fragments)
operations.description: Enrich poly(A)-bearing RNA fragments from the degraded FFPE RNA population; the selected fraction retains the illustrated poly(A)-containing 3′ fragments.
operations.mechanism: Poly(A) selection; the primary paper describes enrichment of mRNA while removing much ribosomal and other non-poly(A) RNA.
operations.information_effect: Restricts the RNA population copied into the library to a poly(A)-enriched subset. The upstream portions already lost through degradation are not reconstructed.

operations.label: Anneal primer
operations.description: Anneal the P7-linked oligo(dT) RT primer to the depicted poly(A) end of each selected RNA fragment, producing the primer–RNA complex.
operations.mechanism: Oligo(dT) hybridization to the poly(A) tract; the primer carries the P7 handle and terminal degenerate positions shown in the legend.
operations.information_effect: Places the primer-derived P7 handle at the intended transcript 3′ end for directional copying. The reported internal-priming and slippage limitations qualify this enrichment.

operations.label: 2nd strand cDNA synthesis
operations.description: Synthesize the complementary DNA strand from the first-strand product, changing the substrate to double-stranded cDNA for linker ligation.
operations.mechanism: Second-strand cDNA synthesis; the schematic does not name an enzyme or show internal substeps.
operations.information_effect: Preserves the transcript-derived insert and the P7-associated end in a double-stranded DNA substrate.

operations.label: Ligate P5 linker
operations.description: Ligate the P5 linker to the cDNA end opposite the existing P7 handle, producing the P5/P7-linked blue duplex and final cDNA endpoint.
operations.mechanism: P5-linker ligation to double-stranded cDNA; P7 was introduced earlier through the RT primer.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second library handle and preserves orientation: P7 at the poly(A)-associated end, P5 opposite it. method_scopes.rationale: The card title, matching collection-page heading/caption, and single labeled route resolve the target as 3Seq, styled 3SEQ in Beck et al. All five local operations apply to the depicted FFPE implementation; the primary caption confirms that this already-degraded RNA proceeds to cDNA without added fragmentation. Fresh-frozen use is described in text and the primary paper but has no branch in this assigned diagram. TruSeq RNA Access is a catalogue-associated kit; PAS-Seq and other methods discussed in related sources are not schematic targets. The collection also lists a Riemondy et al. 3Seq application and mentions HITS-CLIP and miRNA-Seq used in that study. This is catalogue-only application evidence; no Riemondy publication/metadata source is present in the supplied registry, so it cannot receive a separate publication PaperMatch or support the scoped FFPE chemistry. Its unshown assays do not enlarge the extraction target.
